Getting Started

This guide will help you take your first steps with the Eisenhower Portfolio Manager system.

1. Logging In

When you first access the system, you will see a login screen. Enter the username and password provided by your system administrator.

After logging in for the first time, you will be prompted to change your password. Choose a strong password that you can remember.

2. Understanding Your Role

Your system administrator assigns you a role that determines what you can do in the system. The available roles are:

Admin Full system access. Can manage all users, configure security, and perform administrative tasks.

Manager Can create and manage portfolios, projects, and tasks. Can assign team members and manage resources.

Member Can create and edit tasks within assigned portfolios. Can update progress and report blockers.

Viewer Read-only access to data for which they have clearance. Cannot modify any data.

3. Your Daily Cockpit

After logging in, you land on your Daily Cockpit — your personal dashboard. Here you will see:

  • Active Tasks — Tasks assigned to you that are not yet complete.

  • Focus Queue — Tasks prioritised by their position on the critical path.

  • Claimable Tasks — Placeholder tasks that you can volunteer to take on.

  • Upcoming Deadlines — Tasks due within the next 48 hours.

  • Blockers — Issues that are preventing progress on your tasks.

4. Navigating the System

The main navigation menu on the left provides access to all features:

  • Dashboard — High-level project statistics and activity feed.

  • Programmes — Browse and manage programme hierarchies.

  • Schedule — View and edit project timelines.

  • Resources — Manage people, equipment, and facilities.

  • Reports — Generate and export reports.

  • Settings — Configure your display preferences.

5. Understanding Security Classifications

The Eisenhower system handles classified data. Each piece of information carries a security classification:

  • OFFICIAL — Standard information.

  • OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE — Information that could cause damage if disclosed.

  • SECRET — Information that could cause serious damage if disclosed.

  • TOP SECRET — Information that could cause exceptionally grave damage.

You can only see data at or below your clearance level. If you encounter a ghost node (shown with redacted data), it means you lack clearance for that item but have clearance for items beneath it.

6. Getting Help

If you need help while using the system:

  • Use the Help Center (accessible from the navigation menu) for quick reference guides on specific topics.

  • Contact your system administrator for account or access issues.

  • Refer to this user guide for detailed feature documentation.
